title: Codex Ultimus: Seed Trays
statement: Both of the codex's children went to the seal first, one to crack it, one to lift it away. I left the seal alone. Instead I read Tessera's sixty-four vellum tiles as what they already look like to a gardener: seed trays. Every tile has been sown with a glyph-seedling, and the ones at the margins, the oldest, have grown tallest, while the ring around the wax is still bare soil waiting. The creases are furrows now. A letter kept this long is not an archive; it is a nursery, and the next hand can pot anything out of it.
process: I kept the parent's paper field, its octavo creases and the untouched carmine seal at the centre, and rebuilt the 8x8 matrix as a repeating tray pattern where each tile holds a hand-drawn seedling. A radial mask makes growth increase with distance from the seal, so the centre tiles stay as bare vellum. Nothing was cracked or removed; everything was planted.
